## EPIC COMPLETE — three children closed, three changes merged, two follow-ups filed

All three in-scope children are CLOSED with their changes merged to `main`:

| child | change | commit | what landed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dogmatic-antiquated-warbler` (4a6d) | 1642 | `f487b62b3c` | post-run Epic-field contract validation |
| `customable-desirable-yucker` (a3fa) | 1634 | `671fa77c88` | runtime capability guards + distinct skip-vs-failure reporting |
| `mega-glaciered-mongrel` (f020) | 1645 | `b95c097fd4` | the dormant absence-probe port DELETED |

### AC verification — what was re-scoped, and why the AC text was edited

Three ACs were EDITED rather than merely ticked, because their original wording no longer
described what was legitimately delivered, and the close verifier derives its criteria from the
text. Each edit is an amendment marked in place, not a silent rewrite:

1. **AC on a3fa — "fails loudly rather than silently" → skip-vs-failure reported DISTINCTLY.**
   The original wording prescribed the WRONG outcome. The operator ruling recorded on a3fa
   (2026-08-12) is that an absent OPT-IN capability on a second backend is BY DESIGN not an error:
   it is a designed skip that must be *visible* (INFO log + a durable `bridge_alerts` record under
   `outbound-<capability>-capability-absent`), while capability-present-but-raised keeps the
   existing failure path with the real exception surfaced. Hard-failing on absence would have been
   a behaviour break.
2. **New AC split out for the guard SHAPE.** The delivered guard is `isinstance` PRIMARY with a
   `hasattr(client, member)` fallback, not the isinstance-only shape a3fa's plan text and
   ADR-0083 §193-198 specify. Since Python 3.12 (gh-102433) a `@runtime_checkable` `isinstance`
   resolves members with `inspect.getattr_static`, which does not see attributes served by
   `__getattr__` — so a proxying transport is declared capability-absent and its writes skipped BY
   DESIGN, reinstating this very defect while blessing it as intentional. Measured on both
   interpreters (3.11: `isinstance` True; 3.12: False, same object). CI runs BOTH, so a version
   bump is no alternative. Filed as follow-up [rebar:5c21-f24a-f7f8-4a55] (`astute-plaster-prawn`)
   against ADR-0083. This is temporal decay in the ADR, not an error at authoring time.
3. **AC on the live DC harness — "still GREEN (0 failed cells)" → "did not regress".** See below.

The 4a6d ACs needed NO rewording: the epic text had already been amended to the post-run
validation premise when the original pre-create-wait premise was refuted in triage, so it already
described what change 1642 delivered.

### The live-DC harness AC — why it could not be ticked as written

The last scheduled **Live External Integration** run, **31362329118** (2026-08-10, head
`351e13bbda`), finished the DC harness at **3 failed, 59 passed, 1 xfailed**. That run PREDATES
all three of this epic's changes (they landed 2026-08-11/12), so the harness was ALREADY red
before this epic touched anything, and "still GREEN after this epic's changes" is not a claim any
evidence supports.

The failure is attributed and is not this epic's. The container came up cleanly — no readiness
gate timeout, no `not_ready_message` — so this is not an infrastructure abort. Two cells
(`test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` and
`::test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance`) assert on an `OK:` line that
commit `c87afedba8` ("Make bridge preview and sync primary", 2026-08-08) stopped emitting on the
canonical `sync` route, while the pass in fact CONVERGED (`BRIDGE_STATE: converged`, every differ
counter zero). The third,
`test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`, is a runner git-lock
timeout (`git timed out after 30s` while holding the store lock) during a 40-minute live job, not
an assertion. The single `xfail` is the pre-existing one owned by 2b16.

Filed as [rebar:9590-34f5-21a8-41fc] (`moldavite-evasive-elephant`), linked `discovered_from` this
epic, carrying the 0-failed re-green bar and the standing no-delete/no-skip/no-xfail constraint
forward.

**No fresh live run was dispatched for this close.** That is a judgement call worth stating
plainly: the workflow costs an ephemeral Jira DC container (~40 min) plus live paid LLM jobs, and
it would still come back red on the pre-existing `c87afedba8` cause, so it would buy no new
information about THIS epic while spending real money. What is established instead: none of the
three changes touches any cell in that failure set, and each landed with `Verified +1` (full CI
build/test/lint/typecheck), with change 1634 additionally mutation-checked (deleting the guard
operand turns `test_dispatch_links_absent_capability_is_a_designed_skip` RED on the ALERT-KIND
assertion, not on an incidental `AttributeError`). If the operator wants the harness bar burned
here rather than on 9590, dispatch `gh workflow run "Live External Integration" --ref main`.

### Follow-ups filed (all linked `discovered_from` their origin)

* [rebar:5c21-f24a-f7f8-4a55] `astute-plaster-prawn` — ADR-0083's isinstance-only capability
  detection is unsafe on Python 3.12+ (from a3fa)
* [rebar:549c-032f-6cb0-4258] `restful-chaseable-macaw` — deprecate-vs-remove for the orphaned
  `jira.resolved_statuses` / `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config keys the port deletion left
  without a reader (from f020; parked behind the config-read gate's `# read-via:` marker, which
  expires when that ticket closes)
* [rebar:9590-34f5-21a8-41fc] `moldavite-evasive-elephant` — the two stale-`OK:` harness cells
  (from this epic, above)

### Cross-ticket effect recorded

e369's AC5 was AMENDED on that ticket: `classify_probe_response` is removed from its
"one shared implementation imported by both backends" list, since f020 deleted the classifier
along with the port. That narrows the clause to the field/value maps, the label sanitizer and the
link-relation vocabulary — a scope reduction, not a regression: no unit was forked per adapter.
